reason: The hypothesis directly transfers the specific finding from P7, P13, and P15—that adding 0.5 at.% W to AlCoCrFeNi improves high-temperature wear resistance via lattice distortion and W-rich phases—to a CoCrFeNi matrix, without a new mechanism or integration of other evidence. The proposed mechanism (lattice distortion at low T, W-enriched glaze layer at high T) is taken almost verbatim from those passages, and the predicted outcome restates their reported results as a prediction. The change from AlCoCrFeNi to CoCrFeNi is a minor compositional variation with no stated justification for why the effect should transfer in the absence of Al.
copied_elements: Adding W to a CoCrFeNi-based HEA to improve high-temperature wear resistance
Formation of W-rich intermetallic compounds or phases
Protective oxide/glaze layer formation at high temperatures
Reduced friction coefficient and wear loss at 800 °C
Dual benefit of low-temperature hardening and high-temperature oxide protection
